resources.string: The daemon can keep the last network map on the device and connect to your devices from it at start, before the coordination server answers — so the tailnet comes up even when the server is blocked or slow. The server turns this on per device with the cache-network-maps node attribute; a tailnet policy can withhold it with disable-cache-network-maps. Until the server answers, the saved map is all the device knows: new or removed devices, changed access rules and who is online catch up only then.
Start from the saved network map
Off, the saved map is not used and is deleted at the next contact with the server. Changing this restarts the connection.
The server lets this device keep a map.
The server does not let this device keep a map; it starts without one.
No contact with the coordination server: running on the map the device has.
Connect to see whether the server allows it.
Deletes the saved maps of every account. The next map from the server is saved again while the switch above is on.
